newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bk of E.Asia bullish on Hong Kong future.
newsitem.headline: Bk of E.Asia bullish on Hong Kong future.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd deputy chairman and chief executive David Li said on Monday he was bullish on the future of Hong Kong which reverts to China in July.
"I am extremely bullish about Hong Kong and its future," Li told a news conference.
"I think we have a very strong foundation and I basically believe that Hong Kong will continue for a certain growth," he said.

The government estimates the territory's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 5.1 percent in the third quarter of last year, versus 4.6 percent in the second quarter. It forecast a 4.7 percent rise in GDP for 1996.
"And I also believe that Hong Kong will not only become a financial centre for South China," he said. "Hong Kong is already a financial centre for Asia-Pacific."

As Britain will hand the colony back to communist China on July 1, some people feel uncertain about the territory's future. Li, who was recently in Beijing meeting Chinese officials, said the Chinese economy was doing well itself.

"I feel that China has already had a soft landing, as far as inflation is concerned. I think...it's likely that they will have a further cut in the interest rate and the economy is moving in the right direction," he said.
The resolution of Sino-U.S. textile trade dispute was also a positive development, he added.
"My concern about Hong Kong is our costs of living," Li said. "I think that our costs, particularly our property prices, are out of line with the rest of the world, apart from Japan,"
He called on the territory's post-handover leader-designate Tung Chee-hwa to address the issue.
